<Rep. Robert C. "Bobby" Scott, Rep. Frederica S. Wilson, Rep. Suzanne Bonamici, Rep. Mark Takano, Rep. Mark DeSaulnier, Rep. Jahana Hayes, Rep. Summer L. Lee, Rep. Adelita S. Grijalva>: This is extremely concerning considering the damage to institutions that the President has been able to hand select Board majorities, particularly the Kennedy Center and the U.S. Peace Institute.\42\ Based on these real-world examples, it is not beyond the pale to hypothesize that a Trump-led Board would not hesitate to rename this the Trump/Truman--or just Trump-- Foundation Program.\43\ Based on concerns raised by these provisions, Ranking Member Scott offered two amendments that would seek to prevent the President and his handpicked board for exerting undue influence. The first amendment would delay the effective date of this act until after President Trump left office. The amendment also made clear the Board members would not have the power to rename the Foundation or to award scholarships in the name of anyone besides President Truman. The amendment was defeated on a party line vote. The second amendment recognized the reality that the sponsor of H.R. 7894, the bill that would dissolve the Board, is a current Member of the Board. The amendment would prohibit any Member of Congress who supported the dissolution of the current Board of Trustees would not be allowed to serve as a Trustee constituted under this bill if it was made law. This seemed to prevent what would be rather inherent conflict of interest a Member might have to vote to create vacancies they could then fill. This amendment was also defeated on a party line vote.

Times, Mar. 17, 2026, https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/17/us/politics/ institute-of-peace-trump.html.
\43\Id.; see, e.g., The Associated Press, Trump is fighting the Institute of Peace in court. Now, his name is on the building, NPR, Dec. 4, 2025, https://www.npr.org/2025/12/04/g-s1-100576/trump-institute-of-peace-name.
Section 4 of the bill amends the portion of law that determines how Truman Scholars are selected. Like section 3, some edits are non-controversial such as re-wording of requirements currently found in regulation.\44\ But the bill includes new statutory dictates on how the Regional Review Panels are composed, requiring the Foundation to ensure party parity among the members of these panels. Further, the bill would prohibit a scholar from having been a ``leader, officer, director, or organizers'' of a student organization that was suspended or expelled from campus. This is an obvious attempt to disqualify certain students affiliated with campus groups that were suspended or expelled from their schools in the wake of post-Oct. 7 protests in such a way that would not allow these students to explain or distinguish themselves in fairly important ways.\45\ Finally, section 4 prohibits the Scholarship from disfavoring candidates who intend to pursue a Masters of Business Administration (MBA) degree. The Truman Scholarship program is designed to award scholars who intend to pursue a career in public service.\46\ Regulations that govern the program require that ``Scholars must include in their submission to the Foundation a statement of interest in a career in public service that specifies in detail how their graduate program and their overall educational and work experience plans will realistically prepare them for their chosen career goal in government or elsewhere in public service.''\47\ The Foundation has found that in general MBA degree programs will not meet this threshold, and admittedly the Foundation has not gone out of its way to demonstrate that this is not a hard-and-fast rule.\48\ But there are many scholars with MBA degrees. Recognizing that this disfavor is not an accurate description of how the Foundation handles MD or MBA applicants, Ranking Member Scott offered an amendment striking these provisions as unnecessary. The amendment was defeated on a party-line vote.
\44\Compare H.R. 7894 Page 7, Line 19-Page 8, Line 6 to 45 C.F.R. 1801.21.

There are, of course, exceptions. If you believe that you fall into that category, you must make the connection between the MBA and your future career in public service very clear to the committee.''); see also 45 C.F.R. 1801.32 (``Truman Scholars at the graduate level may use Foundation support to study at any accredited college or university in the United States or abroad that offers graduate study appropriate and relevant to their public service career goals.''(emphasis added)).
The bill makes further changes that will infuse politics into the program. Section 6 would revise the selection of the Foundation's Executive Secretary, and just as Section 3 dissolved the current Board, section 6 would remove the current Executive Secretary in the bill's efforts to ``clean house.'' This action is taken with no suggestion of improper actions by the current holder of the position and would allow \2/3\ of the board to elect a new Executive Secretary. Again, as the President appoints eight members to the Board and the Secretary of Education sits ex officio, this would allow for an Executive Secretary hand-picked by the President's hand-picked Board.
Section 7 would require the Foundation to maintain press releases, program announcements, biographies of scholarship recipients on their website. This is based on the fact that the Foundation put these documents behind a password-protected wall after AEI and The College Fix used these documents as ``evidence'' in their ``analysis'' of Truman scholars. As the Right has already shown a willingness to dox and misconstrue this data to give impressions of bias, section 7 would only make this easier, and likely have a chilling effect on certain students from applying to be scholars in the first place. Section 8 establishes effective dates of the bill and holds harmless previous the awards of previous Truman Scholars.

CONCLUSION
Based on dubious research from conservative-leaning foundations and publications, this Committee has engaged in politically charged oversight of the Truman Foundation. At a time when Americans are finding it harder to afford a higher education, the Majority has written multiple letters, held hearings, and marked up a bill based on a program that serves approximately 60 students annually. This is not a judicious use of this Committee's time and resources. Further, the changes to law presented in this bill will exacerbate the problem the Majority claims to be solving, the insertion of politics into a public service scholarship program.
For the reasons stated above, all Committee Democrats present unanimously opposed H.R. 7894 when the Committee on Education and Workforce considered it on March 17, 2026. We urge the House of Representatives to do the same.
